programme.desc: In this episode of "Why'd They Wear That?," hosts Clinton Kelly and Stacy London explore the visual style of Tony Scott's 1983 cult classic "The Hunger," featuring Catherine Deneuve and David Bowie as centuries-old vampires. The hosts examine nine distinct fashion moments from the film, analyzing how costume designer Milena Canonero masterfully blends 1940s silhouettes with 1980s sensibilities. They discuss iconic pieces including leather catsuits, garrison caps, oversized blazers, trenches, and statement accessories like an ornate salamander brooch. The conversation highlights how the costumes reveal character, wealth, and sophistication, while exploring the film's enduring influence on fashion and the practical challenges of recreating these looks today.

Canora shares how broth became central to his wellness journey and cooking philosophy. The hosts and guest prepare a roasted half-chicken with a pan sauce made from brodo, demonstrating how quality broth elevates home cooking. The episode includes a NYC food-themed "Chew It or Screw It" game and explores Canora's approach to seasonal, farm-to-table cooking. Canora reveals creative applications of broth, including savory beverage variations with olive oil, bacon fat, and other ingredients.

programme.title: Chewed Up
programme.desc: In this episode of Chewed Up, hosts Clinton Kelly, Carla Hall, and Michael Symon explore the world of peanut butter through a blind taste test of six popular brands, discussing texture, flavor, and baking applications. They identify standout options across smooth, chunky, and nostalgic categories, then demonstrate two versatile peanut butter recipes: a quick Asian-inspired spicy peanut sauce made with soy sauce, sesame oil, rice wine vinegar, and chili crisp served over udon noodles, and an elegant dessert of pitted dates stuffed with peanut butter, drizzled with dark chocolate, and finished with flaked sea salt. Both recipes highlight peanut butter's versatility as a protein-rich ingredient for quick meals, snacks, and desserts.

programme.title: Chewed Up
programme.desc: On Chewed Up, hosts Clinton Kelly, Carla Hall, and Michael Symon tackle two bagel-focused segments. First, Clinton demonstrates how to make jalapeño popper–stuffed bagels—a pull-apart recipe featuring cream cheese, cheddar, bacon bits, and jalapeños baked until melty and shareable. Then the hosts conduct a blind taste test of five frozen bagel brands commonly found in supermarket freezers, comparing texture, chew, and flavor to determine which best approximates a quality New York–style bagel. The episode highlights how different formulations freeze and reheat differently, with surprising winners emerging from lesser-known brands.

programme.title: Chewed Up
programme.desc: Carla Hall and Michael Symon sit down with legendary pit master Myron Mixon, the winningest competitor in barbecue history with over 200 grand championship wins. Mixon walks viewers through his famous baby back ribs recipe, proving that great barbecue doesn't require exotic ingredients or advanced chemistry. Starting with St. Louis spares from any grocery store, he covers essential techniques including membrane removal, a simple juice-based injection using apple and peach juice, a three-component dry rub, and a controlled smoking process at 275 degrees. Myron emphasizes that tenderness and proper seasoning come from technique and consistency rather than complicated methods. The episode includes discussion of his journey in competitive barbecue, his philosophy on staying focused on what you do best, and four giveaways featuring his signature rubs, sauces, and cookbooks.

programme.title: Chewed Up

The hosts discuss memorable dishes they've encountered—from miso chocolate cake to caramelized onions with maple—and share techniques for adapting recipes based on ingredient quality and personal palate. A playful game challenges the hosts to create dishes using random savory and sweet ingredients, resulting in creative proposals like sun-dried tomato pide with hot honey and cherry bourbon caramelized onion sauce.

programme.title: Simply Symons
programme.desc: In the debut episode of Simply Symons, Michael Symon welcomes viewers into his Venice, California front yard alongside his wife Liz Symon and their friend Olivia Annacone Cisic for an unfiltered, laid-back cookout. Celebrating Cinco de Mayo, Michael prepares simple yet flavorful black cod fish tacos on a plancha, walking through his approach to seasoning, cooking fish by sight, and building a bright, crunchy slaw with cabbage, citrus, and charred poblanos. The conversation flows easily as the trio shares cooking tips, debates ingredients like corn versus flour tortillas, and jokes about knife sharpening habits, cilantro preferences, and home cooking realities. Liz complements the meal with a refreshing jalapeño margarita, balancing heat with fresh lime juice, simple syrup, and a hint of orange liqueur, while adding her own creative twist with lemon and bitters. Throughout the episode, the group emphasizes flexibility in cooking—encouraging viewers to adjust flavors, garnishes, and spice levels to their own tastes. Lighthearted banter continues as they assemble tacos, discuss plating ideas, and highlight optional additions like crema and avocado. The episode wraps with a taste test, enthusiastic reactions to both the tacos and cocktail, and a reminder that great food doesn’t have to be complicated—just fresh, simple, and made with joy.

programme.title: They Volunteered for This: Merrill's Marauders
programme.desc: MERRILL'S MARAUDERS: THEY VOLUNTEERED FOR THIS tells the fascinating story of a group of World War II soldiers known as Merrills Marauders who were one of the most heroic and least known combat units to serve in the war. Fighting in Burma in 1944-1945 under the legendary General Frank Merrill, the Marauders were all volunteers who specialized in hit and run tactics in the jungles and mountains of the region. In this documentary, veterans recount the brazen tactics and clever strategies they used to outwit and defeat the enemy. They were not supplied very well and had to use mules to move from place to place to carry what supplies they did have. The Japanese always thought the 3,000 soldiers were a group of 15,000 due to their success of being everywhere at every time, and because of the damage and casualties they were able to inflict. What the Marauders did was miraculous considering the environment in which they fought and the determined enemy they fought against. In 2022 the Marauders received the Congressional Gold Medal in recognition of their sacrifice and accomplishments. Narrated by television news icon Tom Brokaw, the documentary includes vivid recollections of the veterans who volunteered for the mission, enhanced by archival combat footage from the war.

programme.title: Unsettled History: America, China, and the Doolittle Tokyo Raid
programme.desc: The Doolittle Raiders were one of the most famous American aviation units of World War II. The new documentary UNSETTLED HISTORY: AMERICA, CHINA AND THE DOOLITTLE TOKYO RAID examines a key moment in American/Chinese history, exploring how the two sides recall a daring 1942 raid on Tokyo, and how this shared event is remembered in different ways, the reasons for this divergence and what lessons it may hold for today. In the film, the memory of the Raiders is kept alive by their children and grand-children, as well as by descendants of the courageous Chinese men and women who rescued many of them from likely capture, torture, or even death at the hands of the Japanese military. On April 18, 1942, sixteen U.S. Army aircrews embarked on their first combat mission. They had enough fuel to reach their targets -- military and industrial sites in Tokyo and five other Japanese cities but not enough to go much farther. Even if they somehow made their way to the relative safety of China, no one knew they were coming. In 2018, the children of the Doolittle Raiders visited China, to literally walk in their fathers footsteps. But is this mission remembered in China as heroic or misguided? And what kind of reception did they receive at a time when US/China relations were bad, and getting worse? One historical event, two different narratives.

programme.title: Above and Beyond
programme.desc: ABOVE AND BEYOND highlights one of the most compelling escape and survival stories from World War II that of former Rhode Island Governor Bruce Sundlun (1920-2011). Sundlun, a U.S. Army Air Corps pilot, flew a B-17 bomber nicknamed the Damn Yankee on a dozen combat missions during World War II. On December 1, 1943, Sundlun's unlucky 13th mission would take him (a Jewish-American) and his crew into Hitler's backyard the heart of Germany's industrial Ruhr Valley. While on the mission, the bomber drew heavy fire from German fighter planes and crashed in a field in the Nazi-occupied Belgian town of Jabbeke. By nightfall, Sundlun remained the only member of his 10-man crew not killed or captured by the Germans. Muddied and bloodied, Sundlun eluded the Germans by hiding in plain sight face down between a row of crops. He soon found refuge in a local farmhouse, his wounds tended by a local family. For the next several days, courageous Catholic priests and local members of the French Resistance sheltered Sundlun and provided him with fake identity papers. With help from a vast underground network, Bruce fled to occupied France, where he joined the Resistance (under the code name Salamander) and assisted them in their fight against the Nazis. Eventually smuggled into neutral Switzerland, Sundlun would spy for the U.S. Office of Strategic Services (OSS), the precursor to the CIA, tasked with communicating with French Resistance and German officers looking to surrender.The documentary unfolds as Sundlun's daughter Kara retraces his wartime journey. In Jabbeke, Kara meets author and local historian Luc Packo, as well as witnesses to her father's plane crash, who still celebrate Sundlun's contribution to their country's liberation.

programme.title: War Journal: The Incredible World War II Escape of Major Damon Rocky Gause
programme.desc: The thrilling true story of a nearly impossible escape from prison camp during World War II. In 1942, American airman Rocky Gause escaped a prison camp on the Bataan Peninsula, swam to nearby Corregidor Island, and then sailed with U.S. serviceman William Osborne in a leaky fishing boat 3,200 miles from the Philippines to Australia. Despite facing typhoons, constant threats from Japanese ships, submarines and airplanes, a lack of water and food, and even a visit to the worlds largest leper colony, both men survived to recount their harrowing 52-day ordeal. Filmed in Bataan, Corregidor, and in Manila, the documentary features the journals of Gause and Osborne, archival footage and photos, and interviews with relatives and Army associates. It is narrated by three-time Emmy Award-winning actor Chandler Massey, and actor Kyle Chandler (Argo, Zero Dark Thirty and Carol) provides the voice of Rocky.

programme.title: Dad's Secret War: France 1944
programme.desc: Narrated by actor Kevin Bacon, Dad’s Secret War: France 1944 focuses on two top-secret World War II organizations – the OSS (Office of Strategic Services) and the British SOE (Special Operations Executive), American and British organizations responsible for silent, unseen, highly classified missions of critical importance to defeating the Nazis. The documentary shares the riveting, true story of an American who joined the British SOE and was parachuted into France with a small team just after D-Day to organize the French Resistance into a cohesive army. The mission was to stop Germany's most feared troops from reaching Normandy in the days after the D-Day landings of June 6, 1944.
